subject: hoverPickup
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: militarized pickup converted to hover thrusters.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning a static hover-pickup model built from parts and extrusions, sized roughly 5.2m long and 2m wide, with thruster pods positioned so their lowest points rest at ground level.

I'm laying out the chassis and body as an extruded side profile — tracing a polygon from rear bumper through bed, cab, windshield, hood, to the nose — to form the truck's silhouette in one swept hull.

For the finish I'll go with a dark gunmetal body with neon cyan/magenta cyberpunk accents rather than a military paint job. I need to hollow out the bed though, so I'm adjusting the profile so the bed floor sits lower and adding separate wall and tailgate boxes to create the open cargo area instead of a solid block.

Now I'm adding bed contents like a roll bar, pintle gun, ammo crates, and an angled rocket pod with cylinder tubes, plus working out the dark-glass window geometry -- thin tinted slabs for the side windows and a slanted box for the windshield, calculating the angle needed for the windshield slope.

Positioning the windshield box with a slight lift along its normal to sit just above the hull surface. Now I'm planning the hover thrusters: four nacelles at the corners made of lathe-cylinder housings with glowing cyan downward discs and fan blade textures inside.

Connecting each pod to the chassis via a strut arm and fender wing, then shaping the pod shell with an open bottom and a textured glow disc facing downward, plus a cyan torus ring at the rim for extra glow.

Now adding support struts linking the pods to the body sides, overlapping intentionally for a solid look, along with an underbelly hover plate glow strip. Then starting on the front with an armored bull bar and cyan headlight glow.

Adding greeble details now: grille slits, hood scoop, roof light bar, antenna, searchlight, military decal numbers, camo patches, neon side stripe, door panel textures with glyphs and warning stripes, plus plans for taillights, license plate, and emblem textures.

For the rear, I'm placing a glowing taillight bar, two horizontal rear booster thrusters with orange glow, a pintle-mounted machine gun with ammo box, and a rocket pod with six tubes positioned on the bed.

Writing camo paint logic...

Now I'm working through the hull extrusion direction and thickness centering, making sure the panel geometry stays aligned along the correct axis. I'm also considering whether to differentiate the cab from the bed with fender flares or a narrower cab shape, but deciding to keep it simpler for now.

I'm planning to split the vehicle into two separate extrudes: a lower body section covering the rear, bed, and hood with one thickness, and a slightly narrower cab extrude layered on top. I'm sketching out the coordinate points for the lower body profile, tracing the rear bottom up through the hood slope and back toward the bed area, though the bed-to-hood transition still needs more work.

Still working out the cab's windshield geometry -- calculating the slope from the cab base up to the roof front point, checking the angle comes out around 58° from horizontal.

Computing the normal offset for the windshield plane gives me a box centered around (0,1.631,0.91) with slight thickness. Now I'm defining the cab's cross-section profile points, adjusting the back edge to be near-vertical to match the vehicle's silhouette.

Working out a small rotated box to approximate the rear window, estimating the slope angle of the back slope at roughly 50 degrees and setting up the rotation matrix for its placement.

Now I'm sketching the side window outlines, estimating pane polygons along the B-pillar by mapping roof curve coordinates at different heights to figure out where the glass edges should sit.

I'll mirror the glass pane across x using the opposite sign, giving it a flat dark navy-teal color without glow. The pods can overlap the hull sides slightly since that's fine visually, and I'll place a door decal on the lower hull flank rather than the cab area.

Now I'm adding neon accent strips along the lower body in magenta and a cyan line along the hood edges, plus headlight bars positioned near the front nose profile.

Placing more vehicle details...

Now I'm adding exterior details: angled armour plates on the hood, a roof light bar with amber/red/blue glow segments, an antenna and satellite dish, a front searchlight cylinder, side mirrors with small glows, door handles and fuel cap, and red glowing tail light bars at the rear.

Working out the truck bed structure: side walls, a tailgate, a dark bed liner floor, and a magenta glow trim along the top of the walls, plus cargo items like stenciled crates, a rocket pod, and a mounted gun, with rear booster cylinders positioned along the back.

Now I'm placing rear thruster cylinders behind the tailgate near the bumper, each with a glowing orange disc facing backward, and adding a magenta glow belly panel along the underside of the hull.

I'm also planning angled pylon struts connecting the pods to the hull, plus swept-back canard fins extruded onto the pods' outer sides using polygon outlines.

Now I'm defining the pod shape itself as a lathed housing profile with a shell wall, leaving the bottom open so the disc underneath is visible.

I'm adjusting the vertical positioning so the lathe bottom, glow disc, and ring torus all sit just above the floor without clipping through it, shifting the whole assembly down until the lowest point is barely touching ground level.

Now I'm fleshing out the hull details: faceted lathe geometry with 8 segments, dark iron metal paint for the main body, and a glowing accent torus band wrapped around the midsection in magenta/cyan, rotated flat to lie horizontally. I'm also adding small intake vent boxes on top plus a thin antenna rod, and designing a radial-bladed fan texture with a cyan glow for the disc surface.

I'm skipping unnecessary rng imports to avoid typecheck issues, and planning extra cyberpunk flourishes like rear exhaust pipes, a license plate decal, door text, and a cluster of antennas at the back of the cab for added detail.

Now I'm figuring out bed accessories — whip antennas with glowing tips, a tow hook, fuel cans, and ammo boxes — plus laying out the rocket pod and its pedestal mount with specific position and tilt values within the truck bed bounds.

Working out rocket pod geometry...

Now I'm designing the pintle gun mount near the pod: a pedestal cylinder, gun body box, barrel rod angled forward, ammo box, and a hexagonal shield plate in front.

I'm placing a shield box in front of the gun, then positioning crates and fuel cans around it so they don't overlap with the gun's footprint or barrel path, and adjusting roll bar post positions to avoid clashing with the gun assembly.

Now I'm shifting the roll bar to the rear of the vehicle, building an arch frame with posts and a crossbar that can hold small spotlight boxes, making sure the gun fits underneath without collision.

I'm starting to plan the surface textures—a fan disc pattern, a door decal with an identifier and hazard stripe plus an emblem, and a hood emblem design.

I settle on roughly five to six textures total: the hood emblem, a license plate, an "AMMO" crate stencil, and simple flat-glow colors for headlights and taillights, skipping extras like a roof hologram or windshield text. I decide monospace fonts work for any SVG text, and I'm thinking through how to apply glow to textured parts—keeping door decals modestly lit at a lower glow intensity while using white as the base color underneath the colored textures.

Since emissive maps mean unlit areas stay dark regardless, I settle on a glow value around 0.5 for the door decal. I define a simple helper function for building box-shaped parts with color and position options, noting that static models can skip joints entirely since there's nothing to animate. I check the overall height comes to about 2.0 units plus the antenna, and I lay out a color palette using hex codes for gunmetal, dark plate, cyan, magenta, amber, and red accents.

Now I'm working through the paint assignments for each material type, defining a lathe-generated pod shape from an axis-symmetric outline with distinct points to avoid self-intersection, then adding struts and fins as overlapping box and extrusion shapes to connect the pod to the body.

Still adjusting fin placement...

I'll cap the fin height around y=.62 so it extends above the pod without overreaching, then add a small strobe light detail. Writing a reusable box helper for geometry parts and setting up a mirror loop for symmetric placement, with rotations specified in degrees. Starting on texture SVGs next.

Writing SVG code...

Positioning the neon strips on the skirt outer faces in cyan, keeping taillights red, then shaping a hood scoop as an extruded wedge profile with a glowing grille inset.

Adding a cyan glow rod along the hood edges, then sketching the cab roof details including a lathe-built satellite dish dome mounted toward the rear.

I'm designing the roof lightbar with a dark base box and glowing magenta/cyan segment boxes, then adding two forward-facing spotlight cylinders near the front roof edge with their own glow circles.

Next I'm placing antenna rods at the cab's rear corners with small red glow tips, keeping the max height under 2.63, and sketching the side mirrors as thin stalk rods connecting to dark rectangular mirror boxes.

Then I'm checking the windshield box fits within the cab width, adding a tailgate box with a license plate decal and bumper, and placing small tail light boxes on either side of the tailgate at the correct height.

Next I'm positioning rear booster cylinders beneath the bumper with glow discs facing backward, adjusting their z-span so they sit flush against the hull, then adding underbody chassis boxes beneath the hull bottom before moving on to writing the actual rendering code.

I'm importing the glow effect from the kit path and confirming it works with both part meshes and sweep geometries like rods, then setting up a crate texture with hazard stripe patterns drawn via an SVG pattern definition applied across all box faces.
